questions.question: Which architectural and ideological shift characterized the reign of the Khmer Emperor Jayavarman VII in the late 12th and early 13th centuries, distinguishing his rule from earlier monarchs such as Suryavarman II?
options: A transition to Theravada Buddhism accompanied by the abandonment of urban temple complexes in favor of decentralized forest monasteries.
The adoption of Mahayana Buddhism and the construction of the Bayon temple, featuring massive face-towers representing the monarch as the Bodhisattva Lokeshvara.
The complete purge of Indian religious traditions in favor of indigenous ancestor worship, marked by the destruction of Hindu reliefs at Angkor Wat.
The institutionalization of Sunni Islam through maritime diplomatic alliances, resulting in the conversion of the royal court.

questions.question: Under the administrative system established by the Mughal Emperor Akbar, how did the mansabdari system function to organize imperial governance?
options: It created a hereditary military nobility that owned permanent, tax-exempt land grants independent of imperial revocation.
It established a strictly religious judicial hierarchy responsible for administering Islamic law and managing public endowments.
It assigned non-hereditary numerical ranks (zat and sawar) to civil and military officials, determining their bureaucratic status, salary, and troop obligations.
It functioned as a maritime concession system that leased imperial ports along the Gujarat coast to private mercantile cartels.

questions.question: In the context of the Mongol Empire during the 13th and 14th centuries, what was the primary function of the ortogh institution?
options: A postal relay network of horse stations designed to facilitate rapid imperial communication across Eurasia.
An elite council of tribal leaders convened exclusively to elect a new Supreme Khan at a kurultai.
A written legal code compiled under Genghis Khan to settle disputes between nomadic pastoralists and urban subjects.
A corporate commercial partnership between Mongol elites and foreign merchants formed to pool capital and mitigate long-distance trade risks.

questions.question: In his 1526 correspondence with King John III of Portugal, King Afonso I (Mvemba a Nzinga) of the Kingdom of Kongo primarily protested which aspect of the Portuguese presence in his realm?
options: The unregulated and illegal enslavement of Kongolese subjects, including members of the nobility, by Portuguese merchants.
The refusal of the Portuguese crown to supply European military engineers to assist Kongo's territorial expansion.
The aggressive conversion campaigns conducted by Catholic missionaries aimed at deposing the traditional royal court.
The imposition of heavy Portuguese import duties on Kongolese copper and raffia textiles entering Atlantic trade networks.

questions.question: The 1843 Treaty of the Bogue, signed shortly after the First Opium War, expanded foreign legal and commercial privileges in Qing China primarily by introducing which feature into international relations?
options: The right of foreign powers to establish permanent diplomatic embassies within the Forbidden City in Beijing.
The 'most-favored-nation' clause and formal legal extraterritoriality for British subjects within treaty ports.
The total transfer of imperial maritime customs collection to a foreign-led administrative board.
The legal protection and tax exemption of the opium trade throughout all interior Chinese provinces.
